The Finnish treatment produced substantially higher life satisfaction and lower economic and mental stress, but administrative data showed no major employment effect, while other analyses found a small employment increase whose causal interpretation was weakened by simultaneous policy changes. As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity. As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.  Canada provides suggestive evidence of longer-term social benefits through the earlier Manitoba Mincome experiment, whose later analysis associated guaranteed income with unchanged work incentives, lower hospitalisation, and higher school completion, although these results came from a 1970s experiment rather than the post-2015 Ontario pilot.
